facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of an enlarging, intermittently painful, purplish lump in her left ear canal
cracking and pus-filled sores at the site
a 3.5 × 2.5 cm purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
irregular, friable surface and bleeding on minimal contact
Contrast-enhanced CT of the mastoids showed a lobulated mass in the cutis and subcutis of the left auricle
extending into the external acoustic canal and into the left parotid space
bilateral level II–IV cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
CT angiography demonstrated marked vascularity of the mass
supplied by branches of the left superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation
a provisional diagnosis of an auricular malignant tumor without a clear histopathological subtype

rationales.F01: The presence of a purplish lump in the ear canal suggests a possible malignant tumor.
rationales.F03: The large size of the mass and its irregular, friable surface suggest a malignant tumor.
rationales.F04: The bleeding on minimal contact suggests a highly vascular tumor, which is consistent with a malignant tumor.
rationales.F05: The presence of a lobulated mass in the cutis and subcutis of the auricle suggests a malignant tumor.
rationales.F08: The marked vascularity of the mass suggests a highly vascular tumor, which is consistent with a malignant tumor.
rationales.F10: The presence of atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation suggests a malignant tumor, but rules out granulomatous inflammation of the ear and pyogenic granuloma of the ear.
rationales.F11: The provisional diagnosis of an auricular malignant tumor without a clear histopathological subtype suggests a malignant tumor, but does not provide enough information to rule in or out specific types of tumors.
